name: brush hair. A person using a comb, brush, or fingers to groom their hair.
cartwheel. A person rotating sideways with arms and legs extended in a wheel-like motion.
catch. A person successfully receiving an object thrown toward them, such as a ball.
chew. A person moving their jaws to break down food or gum in the mouth.
clap. A person striking their palms together to make a sound, often repeatedly.
climb. A person moving upward on a vertical surface, such as a wall, ladder, or tree.
climb stairs. A person ascending a staircase step by step.
dive. A person leaping headfirst into water, usually from a platform or edge.
draw sword. A person pulling a sword out of its sheath.
dribble. A person bouncing a ball continuously, usually while moving.
drink. A person consuming liquid from a container, bottle, glass, or straw.
eat. A person putting food into their mouth and chewing/swallowing.
fall floor. A person collapsing or dropping suddenly onto the ground.
fencing. Two people engaging in a duel with fencing swords (e.g., épée, foil, sabre).
flic flac. A backward handspring performed in gymnastics.
golf. A person swinging a golf club to hit a ball.
handstand. A person balancing upside down with weight supported on the hands.
hit. A person striking an object or another person with hand, object, or tool.
hug. Two people wrapping their arms around each other in an embrace.
jump. A person propelling themselves upward or forward off the ground.
kick. A person striking out with the foot toward an object or target.
kick ball. A person using the foot to strike a ball.
kiss. A person touching lips to another person, cheek, or object.
laugh. A person expressing amusement with facial movement and vocal sound.
pick. A person selecting or lifting up an item from a surface or group.
pour. A person transferring liquid from one container into another.
pullup. A person lifting their body upward on a horizontal bar using arm strength.
punch. A person striking forward with a closed fist.
push. A person exerting force to move something away from themselves.
pushup. A person repeatedly raising and lowering their body with arms while lying face-down.
ride bike. A person moving forward while pedaling and balancing on a bicycle.
ride horse. A person sitting on and directing a horse in motion.
run. A person moving rapidly on foot with both feet leaving the ground during strides.
shake hands. Two people clasping hands and moving them slightly up and down in greeting.
shoot ball. A person attempting to score by throwing or kicking a ball toward a goal.
shoot bow. A person drawing and releasing an arrow from a bow.
shoot gun. A person aiming and discharging a firearm.
sit. A person lowering their body to rest on a chair, bench, or ground.
situp. A person repeatedly lifting the upper body from a lying-down position.
smile. A person curving their lips upward to show pleasure or friendliness.
smoke. A person inhaling or exhaling smoke from a cigarette, cigar, or pipe.
somersault. A person performing a full forward or backward rotation of the body.
stand. A person rising upright with weight supported on the legs.
swing baseball. A person swinging a bat to strike a baseball.
sword. A person holding or wielding a sword in a non-combat context.
sword exercise. A person practicing martial or training movements with a sword.
talk. A person speaking, usually with visible mouth and facial movements.
throw. A person propelling an object through the air with arm motion.
turn. A person rotating their body or changing facing direction.
walk. A person moving forward at a steady pace with alternating steps.
wave. A person raising and moving the hand side-to-side in greeting or farewell.
